best_architecture:
Recommended pattern: a single discord.py v2.x Gateway bot running on the SAME asyncio event loop as the agent orchestrator, with a decoupled inbound-queue + background-worker design.

Library choice: discord.py v2.x (official, actively maintained again since 2021) is the recommended base for an asyncio LLM agent. It is fully native asyncio, has the largest ecosystem, first-class app/slash command support (app_commands), built-in HTTP rate-limit handling with automatic 429 back-off, and is the de-facto base for nearly all existing LLM Discord bots (e.g. jakobdylanc/llmcord). py-cord is a viable drop-in fork with slightly more ergonomic slash-command decorators; hikari is more type-safe/modular but has a steeper learning curve, smaller ecosystem, and no voice support — only choose hikari for large-scale, microservice-style deployments. For Local-Claw (single bot, asyncio orchestrator integration) discord.py is the strongest fit.

Event-loop integration: do NOT spin the bot in a separate thread/loop. discord.py 2.0 added `setup_hook()` and `async with bot:` / `await bot.start(token)` so the bot can be started as a coroutine inside the orchestrator's existing loop via `asyncio.create_task(bot.start(token))` or `await asyncio.gather(bot.start(token), orchestrator.run())`. Sharing one loop avoids cross-thread `run_coroutine_threadsafe` hops and lets the bot and orchestrator await each other's coroutines directly. Use `setup_hook()` to wire the orchestrator handle and `await tree.sync()` for slash commands. Use `discord.ext.tasks.loop(loop=...)` only for periodic background polling.

Inbound async pattern (critical for long-running agent tasks): the Gateway/interaction handler must acknowledge fast and offload work. For slash commands, immediately `await interaction.response.defer(thinking=True)` (Discord requires an ack within 3s; defer extends the window to 15 min) and then hand the task to the orchestrator via an asyncio.Queue or `asyncio.create_task`. The worker runs the agent turn outside the listener's lifetime and posts results back via `interaction.followup` / `channel.send`. This prevents Discord listener timeouts from surfacing as user-visible failures.

Streaming responses: use edit-based streaming — send/defer a placeholder message, accumulate LLM tokens in a buffer, and call `message.edit()` on a THROTTLED cadence (token batching). Edit roughly every ~1-2 seconds (or every N tokens), NOT per-token, to stay under Discord's per-route edit rate limit (~5 edits/sec/channel, with the safe practical target being ~1 edit/sec). Auto-split into new messages when content exceeds the 2000-char limit (4000 with embed description / Nitro). Mark completion visually (e.g. switch embed color to green) when `finish_reason` arrives. Let discord.py's HTTP client absorb any 429s; never hard-code limits — honor `retry_after` headers.

Thread-per-task isolation: for long-running agent sessions, create a Discord thread per task (`channel.create_thread()` or `message.create_thread()`). Each thread isolates one agent session's conversation/streaming output, keeps the parent channel clean, gives natural conversation scoping for context history, and makes it easy to route the eventual completion notification back to the correct thread.

Notifications (webhook vs bot): use the BOT (Gateway) connection for interactive/bidirectional flows (task submission, streaming, approvals) because it can queue and re-send under rate limits and respond to interactions. Use WEBHOOKS as a lightweight fire-and-forget notification sink for one-way 'task complete' pings, especially from worker processes that don't hold a Gateway connection — webhooks let you post to a channel without the bot's full event loop, and support custom username/avatar per message. Pattern: bot for control loop + streaming; webhook for out-of-band completion alerts. Note webhooks have their own rate limits and can fail under load, so the bot path is more robust for guaranteed delivery.

Key design decisions that matter most: (1) one shared asyncio loop, no threads; (2) fast ack + deferred background worker so the 3s/15min interaction windows are never the failure mode; (3) throttled edit-streaming with token batching to respect the 5 edits/sec limit; (4) message-length-aware auto-splitting; (5) thread-per-task for session isolation; (6) bot-for-control / webhook-for-notifications split.
reference_papers: LLM-Based Human-Agent Collaboration and Interaction Systems: A Survey (Feng et al. 2025) - arxiv:2505.00753 - taxonomy of synchronous vs asynchronous human-agent interaction and conversation/observation/shared-message-pool communication modes directly relevant to chat-channel agent UX

Overhearing LLM Agents: A Survey, Taxonomy, and Roadmap (2025) - arxiv:2509.16325 - argues an agent software library should support async programming plus mobile-style notifications/haptics; informs the notification + non-intrusive intervention design

AsyncVoice Agent: Real-Time Explanation for LLM Planning and Reasoning (2025) - arxiv:2510.16156 - asynchronous architecture decoupling a streaming LLM backend from the conversational frontend so narration/inference run in parallel; supports the defer+background-worker+streaming pattern [uncertain - voice-focused, applies by analogy to Discord text streaming]
Human-Centered LLM-Agent User Interface: A Position Paper (2024) - arxiv:2405.13050 - design principles for LLM-agent user interfaces where the agent proactively proposes interaction schemes

AutoGen: Enabling Next-Gen LLM Applications via Multi-Agent Conversation (Wu et al. 2023) - arxiv:2308.08155 - conversation-driven multi-agent orchestration model; background reference for the orchestrator the Discord connector fronts [uncertain - not Discord-specific]
reference_repos: jakobdylanc/llmcord - the most popular ready-to-run Discord LLM chat bot (~200 lines, single file); fully async discord.py, streamed responses via throttled message.edit that turn green on completion, auto message-splitting at length limit, reply-chain conversations, LiteLLM backend for any provider, message-cache to minimize API calls - https://github.com/jakobdylanc/llmcord

Emperornero/llmcord-lmstudio - llmcord fork wired to local LM Studio / Mistral with streamed responses; good reference for local-model + streaming integration - https://github.com/Emperornero/llmcord-lmstudio

hc20k/LLMChat - Discord chatbot with slash-command-driven config (/configure, /model, /message_context_count) and voice support; reference for slash-command task/config surface - https://github.com/hc20k/LLMChat
grqphical/llmcord - Discord LLM client with a plugin architecture (custom API clients via plugins/ folder); reference for pluggable backend design - https://github.com/grqphical/llmcord

DocShotgun/LLM-discordchatbot - Discord bot for local KoboldAI/KoboldCPP/Oobabooga backends with per-user in-memory history and dynamic context trimming - https://github.com/DocShotgun/LLM-discordchatbot
Rapptz/discord.py - the core library itself; reference docs/source for app_commands (slash), discord.ext.tasks, setup_hook, and HTTP rate-limit handling - https://github.com/Rapptz/discord.py
kzndotsh/awesome-discordpy - curated awesome-list of discord.py libraries, extensions, and bot examples - https://github.com/kzndotsh/awesome-discordpy
key_libraries: discord.py - Python - v2.x (>=2.3, latest 2.x as of 2026) - primary asyncio Discord Gateway/REST wrapper; app_commands for slash commands, setup_hook for loop integration, discord.ext.tasks for background loops, built-in 429 rate-limit handling. Recommended base.

py-cord (py-cord) - Python - v2.x - drop-in discord.py fork with more ergonomic @bot.slash_command decorators and ctx.respond/defer; alternative to discord.py if you prefer its slash UX [uncertain - choose one, not both, to avoid namespace conflict]

hikari - Python - v2.x (2.0+) - statically-typed, modular asyncio Discord microframework (GatewayBot + RESTBot); only for large-scale/type-safe deployments; needs a command framework (arc or lightbulb); no voice support
litellm - Python - latest - unified client across OpenAI/Anthropic/Mistral/Ollama/local OpenAI-compatible servers; used by llmcord to decouple the bot from any specific LLM backend
aiohttp - Python - latest (transitive dep of discord.py) - async HTTP, useful directly for posting to Discord webhooks from worker processes that don't hold a Gateway connection

discord.ext.tasks - Python - bundled with discord.py - asyncio.Task helper for periodic background loops with reconnect handling and before_loop/after_loop hooks; accepts a `loop=` arg to bind to an existing event loop

discord-webhook - Python - latest - simple synchronous/async helper for posting completion notifications via Discord webhooks without a full bot connection [uncertain - aiohttp/requests can do this directly; library is optional convenience]
uncertain: reference_papers: no Discord-specific academic papers exist; cited papers cover general async human-agent interaction and apply by analogy
AsyncVoice Agent paper is voice-focused; streaming-decoupling principle transfers to Discord text streaming but was not designed for it
AutoGen is orchestrator/multi-agent background, not a Discord integration reference
py-cord vs discord.py is a one-or-the-other choice; both listed for comparison, not simultaneous use
discord-webhook library is an optional convenience; aiohttp/requests can post webhooks directly
exact current discord.py/py-cord/hikari patch versions not pinned (verify on PyPI at implementation time)
